conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the 4 DECODE images and 2 attached documents (key sheet, address leaf) with the session cookie.
Searched Knox, Letters and Memorials of Allen (1882) text and the web for an edition.
Read the pages: sender is Sir Francis Englefield (cipher signature 70 = Fran.co Englefilol in the key; docket), to the Cardinal of Como, Madrid 15 Nov 1584, not the nuncio Taverna on 1 Jan 1584.
Transcribed the contemporary interlinear decipherments of all cipher runs.
Spot-checked runs against the bound key: chi omega = d e, 69 = Alano, 74 = Ingalaterra, 79 = Roma, 82 = Madrid.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the glossed cipher runs as written above the line at the time (plaintext.txt); the cipher signs were never transcribed and the clear text not transcribed in full (project work)

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): plaintext.txt read through: every glossed cipher run reads as Spanish without holes; the clear text between the runs was never transcribed. Kept as the contemporary decipherment, reviewed B.

outcome.method_basis: Every cipher run on ASV Spagna 31 ff. 210-212 (DECODE R119) carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment, which was transcribed and spot-checked against the key bound as f. 211.
outcome.notes: Read at the time; one short sign group at a hole in f. 210 unglossed. New here: correct sender, recipient and date.

credits.note: interlinear decipherment on ff. 210-212 and the key bound as f. 211

texts.label: R119, Englefield to the Cardinal of Como, Madrid, 15 Nov 1584 (contemporary interlinear decipherment of the cipher runs)
texts.summary: Sir Francis Englefield, the English Catholic exile at the Spanish court, to the Cardinal of Como: he finds the enterprise against England deferred until the Flanders war is over or the Queen of England dies, asks the Pope to open the purse, reports that the Queen of Scots has been put in the custody of three 'most pestiferous Puritans', and asks for a cardinal of the English nation, naming William Allen. The postscript refers Mendoza's objections to 'la grande empresa' to Allen and Persons.

reading_review.note: plaintext.txt read through: it holds the contemporary interlinear decipherment of each cipher run (307 words), and every run reads as clean Spanish (dilatar el negocio; hasta la de Flandes sera acabada, la Reyna de Inglaterra muerta o otra alteracion; don Bernardino de Mendoza after his return from England). The runs are complete; the clear text between them was not transcribed, so whole sentences need the letter's clear text from the images. Audit grade C refined: the C is the missing clear text, not holes in the decipherment.
